successors.name: French Indochina
successors.text: Xiang Khouang province: the Xiang Khouang plateau and the Plain of Jars, the Tai Phuan principality

ledger.x: 13th century: the Tai Phuan settle the Xiang Khouang plateau.

c. 1353: Fa Ngum takes Muang Phuan into Lan Xang. 'In the mid-14th century Muang Phuan was incorporated into the Lan Xang Kingdom under King Fa Ngum'; the page gives no year, 1353 is the lan-xang dossier's date for Fa Ngum's conquests (that dossier quotes its Fa Ngum page: 'In 1353, he conquered Vientiane, Xiang…
1707: Lan Xang divides and Muang Phuan stands apart as a tributary of Luang Prabang.
1832: Dai Viet annexes Muang Phuan as Tran Ninh.

c. 1848: Muang Phuan is again a principality, a vassal of Siam. The page lists 'Vassal to Siam (1848-1893)' and is silent on the end of Vietnamese rule; 1848 is the status list's year, the land and the counterpart are my reading.
1899: the Phuan regions lose their autonomy.

wars.name: Haw invasions of Xiang Khouang
wars.outcome: Haw bands invaded Xiang Khouang in 1874 and carried off population in 1875-1876; no change of border.

certainty.note: The plateau and the Plain of Jars are named; no page gives a frontier, and the principality was under one overlord or another for most of its life.
